sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报 Dealbook 负责商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接观看其中一些不设防、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: November 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Kaitlin Dickerson.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的凯特琳·迪克森。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the founder of Uber has fallen after company shareholders staged a revolt.
sentences.zh: 今天，在公司股东发动叛乱之后，Uber 的创始人黯然下台。

sentences.en: The dramatic hours leading up to Travis Kalanick's resignation.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯·卡兰尼克辞职前那戏剧性的几个小时。

sentences.en: And the opioid crisis already ravaging American cities has escalated to a whole new level with the spread of a drug 50 times more powerful than heroin.
sentences.zh: 而已经肆虐美国城市的阿片类药物危机，随着一种药效是海洛因50倍的新型毒品的蔓延，已经升级到了一个全新的水平。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, June 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月22日，星期四。

sentences.en: You probably didn't sleep at all last night.
sentences.zh: 你昨晚大概根本没怎么睡。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I haven't slept more than two hours in the past 72 hours, I think.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，在过去的72小时里，我大概连两个小时的觉都没睡。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很遗憾。

sentences.en: I hope you get to sleep tonight.
sentences.zh: 希望你今晚能好好睡一觉。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I will hopefully crash soon.
sentences.zh: 我希望待会儿能尽快倒头大睡。

sentences.en: Mike Isaac covers technology for The Times.
sentences.zh: 迈克·艾萨克为《时报》报道科技新闻。

sentences.en: He starts us off Tuesday morning.
sentences.zh: 他从周二早晨开始为我们讲述。

sentences.en: So yeah, so Tuesday morning, Travis is for some reason in downtown Chicago.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，周二早上，不知出于什么原因，特拉维斯正在芝加哥市中心。

sentences.en: He gets contacted by two partners at the firm Benchmark.
sentences.zh: 他联系了 Benchmark 公司的两位合伙人。

sentences.en: So Benchmark is one of Uber's biggest investors.
sentences.zh: Benchmark 是 Uber 最大的投资者之一。

sentences.en: And they sort of want to have an audience with him that morning in Chicago as he's there.
sentences.zh: 他们希望那天早上趁他在芝加哥时能跟他见个面谈谈。

sentences.en: So they're going to travel to Chicago just to meet with him?
sentences.zh: 所以他们特意飞到芝加哥去见他？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So these two partners, Peter Fenton and Matt Kohler, both fly from San Francisco to
sentences.zh: 这两位合伙人，彼得·芬顿和马特·科勒，特意从旧金山飞到

sentences.en: Chicago specifically just to meet with Travis to sit down and have a talk.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥，就是为了跟特拉维斯坐下来面谈。

sentences.en: At this point,
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，

sentences.en: Travis doesn't know what's going on.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯还不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Maybe it's something to do with like an update on, you know, hiring at Uber.
sentences.zh: 也许这跟 Uber 的招聘进展之类的事情有关，你知道的。

sentences.en: He's taken a leave of absence at this point, but he's still sort of involved in very high level discussions.
sentences.zh: 此时他已经开始休假，但仍然参与一些极高层面的讨论。

sentences.en: So 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以早上10点

sentences.en: rolls around Chicago time.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥时间一到，

sentences.en: Travis walks into a room with Matt Kohler, Peter Fenton there, and they present to him a list of investor demands and then a letter of resignation for him to sign that day.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯走进一个房间，马特·科勒和彼得·芬顿在那里，他们向他出示了一份投资者诉求清单，以及一份让他当天签署的辞职信。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So yeah, needless to say, he was not expecting that when he walked into the room.
sentences.zh: 所以，不用说，他走进房间时绝对没有想到这一点。

sentences.en: What happened leading up to that moment?
sentences.zh: 在这之前发生了什么？

sentences.en: Like how did those two investors get there with a letter of resignation in their hands?
sentences.zh: 那两个投资者是怎么带着辞职信出现在那里的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So here's the issue.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: Like for probably four months, Uber has been dealing with this sort of sustained set of crises around the company.
sentences.zh: 大概有四个月的时间，Uber 一直在处理围绕这家公司的一系列持续不断的危机。

sentences.en: You know, there's Susan Fowler, a former employee, published a blog post detailing her history of sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，前员工苏珊·福勒发表了一篇博客文章，详细描述了她遭受性骚扰的经历。

sentences.en: And we broke a story on Uber's use of software to evade law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 我们独家报道了 Uber 使用软件来逃避执法部门监管的事。

sentences.en: And, you know, frankly, it was just affecting how people, if people even wanted to work at Uber anymore.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这甚至开始影响到人们是否还愿意在 Uber 工作。

sentences.en: I was talking to people who were saying there were dozens of employees leaving every week.
sentences.zh: 我当时跟一些人聊过，他们说每周都有几十名员工离职。

sentences.en: So investors at this point were getting pretty nervous.
sentences.zh: 所以当时投资者开始感到相当紧张。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you have this founder, Travis, who refuses to step down and really doesn't actually have to step down because he has this sort of outsized voting control,
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，创始人特拉维斯拒绝下台，而且实际上他也不得不拒绝下台，因为他拥有超乎寻常的投票控制权，

sentences.en: which is by design.
sentences.zh: 这本来就是设计好的。

sentences.en: So initially, investors were on board with that sort of thing, just because
sentences.zh: 所以最初，投资者是支持这种做法的，仅仅因为

sentences.en: Travis had grown Uber to exist in hundreds of cities and dozens of countries around the world.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯让 Uber 发展到了全球数百个城市和几十个国家。

sentences.en: And then at some point that turned and his sort of aggression and unwillingness to yield became a huge liability in their eyes.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时候，情况发生了转变，他的那种好斗和不肯妥协的态度在他们眼里成了一个巨大的负资产。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Travis is handed this letter at 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以特拉维斯在早上10点被递了这封信。

sentences.en: And then what?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: So this is where the day kind of becomes crazy.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一天变得疯狂的地方。

sentences.en: I'm talking to people familiar with the meeting, I would say, throughout the entire day.
sentences.zh: 我一直在和熟悉这场会议的人沟通，可以说是一整天都在联系。

sentences.en: I'm also flying on a plane down to L.A.
sentences.zh: 当时我正坐飞机去洛杉矶，

sentences.en: So I'm like texting.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在发短信。

sentences.en: I'm on airplane Wi-Fi, which is completely awful.
sentences.zh: 我用的是机上 Wi-Fi，简直烂透了。

sentences.en: I have to pull over on the side of the road to get these updates.
sentences.zh: 我不得不把车停在路边来接收这些最新消息。

sentences.en: But Travis is essentially in this meeting, hashing it out with the investors.
sentences.zh: 但特拉维斯基本上就是在这次会议中，和投资者们激烈争论。

sentences.en: And from what I understand, Travis sort of went back and forth.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，特拉维斯的态度反反复复。

sentences.en: You know, initially it was a super intense, aggressive, white-hot, mad sort of meeting.
sentences.zh: 一开始这是一场超级激烈、充满火药味、白热化的疯狂会议。

sentences.en: You know, Travis is a famously sort of aggressive guy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，特拉维斯出了名是个很有攻击性的人。

sentences.en: When you say aggressive, do you think of his yelling at people?
sentences.zh: 你说的有攻击性，是指他会对别人大喊大叫吗？

sentences.en: What exactly does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely he'll yell, you know, or just get really up in their face.
sentences.zh: 是的，他绝对会大吼大叫，或者直接冲到别人脸上去。

sentences.en: He has a habit of pacing to sort of get this frenetic energy out of him.
sentences.zh: 他有一个习惯，就是不停踱步来释放体内那种狂躁的精力。

sentences.en: So as these folks are, as these investors are sitting at the table, you know, Travis is just sort of pacing, intensely talking to them and giving it,
sentences.zh: 所以当这些人坐在桌旁时，特拉维斯就在那儿踱来踱去，情绪激烈地跟他们说话，

sentences.en: rattling off a list of reasons why they're going to get through this and why he should still be there and how, you know, this is a betrayal.
sentences.zh: 滔滔不绝地列举他们为什么能挺过这一关、为什么他应该留下来，以及这有多么像是一场背叛。

sentences.en: You know, at the same time, the investors are sort of like, you need to step aside so we can move on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，与此同时，投资者们的态度则是：你需要靠边站，好让我们继续前进。

sentences.en: So there are breaks throughout the day, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以中间会有一些休息时间，

sentences.en: Travis at one point seems like he's going to fight it.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯有一会儿似乎打算抗争到底。

sentences.en: Then another point, he talks to Arianna
sentences.zh: 但在另一个时刻，他跟阿里安娜·

sentences.en: Huffington, who is on Uber's board of directors and is a close confidant and almost mentor to
sentences.zh: 赫芬顿交谈，她是 Uber 董事会成员，也是特拉维斯的密友兼精神导师般的人物。

sentences.en: Travis.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯。

sentences.en: Arianna kind of talks him down and actually says this might be a good idea.
sentences.zh: 阿里安娜劝导了他，并实际上说这可能是一个好主意。

sentences.en: So he was just sort of back and forth all day.
sentences.zh: 所以他一整天都在摇摆不定。

sentences.en: And then I'm sort of waiting to hear what's going on.
sentences.zh: 然后我一直在等消息，看看到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: I have two versions of a story written, ready to go, whatever he decides.
sentences.zh: 我准备好了两个版本的报道，无论他做出什么决定，随时都可以发。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So in that time, you were able to pull over on the side of the road, get the updates and write not one story, but two.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时候，你不仅能把车停在路边获取最新消息，还能写出两篇完全不同的报道。

sentences.en: Yeah, basically, I had to pull over and write two stories from inside of my car, which was really fun.
sentences.zh: 对，基本上我得把车停在路边，在车里写两篇报道，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: By, I would say 10pm, I start hearing little trickles come out saying you need to call around to see what the latest is.
sentences.zh: 我想大概到晚上10点，我开始听到一些零星的风声，说你需要到处打听一下最新进展。

sentences.en: And then I get a tip that he's agreed to resign, which really blew me away and frankly blew away the investors who approached him for this because they frankly
sentences.zh: 然后我得到一个内幕消息，说他已经同意辞职，这真的让我大吃一惊，坦率地说，也让那些找他谈话的投资者大吃一惊，因为他们原本以为

sentences.en: thought that he was going to fight tooth and nail to the very end.
sentences.zh: 他会拼死抵抗到最后。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So how did Travis respond?
sentences.zh: 那么特拉维斯是怎么回应的？

sentences.en: It was a pretty heartfelt statement.
sentences.zh: 这是一份相当动情的声明。

sentences.en: He said he loves Uber, the company, with all his heart.
sentences.zh: 他说他深爱着 Uber 这家公司。

sentences.en: And he really has made this his entire life for eight years straight.
sentences.zh: 他真的把这当作自己八年来生活的全部。

sentences.en: He hasn't stopped working.
sentences.zh: 他从未停止过工作。

sentences.en: He doesn't take vacations.
sentences.zh: 他从不度假。

sentences.en: He's always, always, always thinking about how Uber can win.
sentences.zh: 他总是、总是、总是想着 Uber 怎样才能赢。

sentences.en: You know, he also talks about how he's going through this difficult time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他还谈到自己正在经历艰难时期。

sentences.en: And, you know, his mother passed away in this sudden boating accident about a month ago.
sentences.zh: 而且，大约一个月前，他的母亲在一场突发的划船事故中不幸去世。

sentences.en: And, and his father was left in critical condition.
sentences.zh: 而且，他的父亲也处于危急状态。

sentences.en: And the guy really is going through it.
sentences.zh: 这家伙确实正在经历一段艰难的时光。

sentences.en: But also, there was a little bit of a tinge of a fight in him.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他的身上也流露出一丝不服输的倔强。

sentences.en: He said, you know, at the same time, I don't want to fight my investors, which are forcing me to step down,
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，与此同时，我不想和逼我辞职的投资者作对，

sentences.en: essentially, kind of like a backhanded acknowledgement that he's being pushed.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这有点像是一种变相承认自己是被逼宫的。

sentences.en: So I'm,
sentences.zh: 所以我在，

sentences.en: I'm doing what is best for the company in the future.
sentences.zh: 我正在做对公司未来最有利的事情。

sentences.en: And that means stepping aside.
sentences.zh: 这意味着退居幕后。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So moving forward, do you expect that Uber can take on a totally different culture, can move away from some of these issues?
sentences.zh: 那么展望未来，你认为 Uber 能呈现一种完全不同的文化吗？能摆脱其中一些问题吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think that the culture is just too entrenched?
sentences.zh: 还是你觉得这种企业文化已经根深蒂固，

sentences.en: And even without Travis, things won't really change.
sentences.zh: 即使没有了特拉维斯，事情也不会有什么真正改变？

sentences.en: I think it's a symbolic moment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个具有象征意义的时刻。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people were not able to get past him.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多人都无法跨过他这一关。

sentences.en: Especially because his personality and identity were so inextricably tied to Uber's brand.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为他的个性和身份与 Uber 的品牌紧密相连，密不可分。

sentences.en: But you know, like, there are a lot of people inside of Uber who kind of want to see themselves
sentences.zh: 但你知道，Uber 内部有很多人希望把公司看作是一家成熟的企业，

sentences.en: as a mature company, you know, like we are on par with a Facebook or a Google or an Apple in the valley.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像我们在硅谷可以和 Facebook、谷歌或苹果平起平坐一样。

sentences.en: And we don't have to act like these bros in Silicon Valley that are just doing a startup in their garage anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不再需要表现得像硅谷那些只会在车库里搞初创公司的兄弟一样。

sentences.en: So I think I think the mood right now is probably hopeful, despite, you know, all the chaos of the past few weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以我想目前的心情可能充满希望，尽管经历了过去几周的所有混乱。

sentences.en: And Mike, how long have you been covering Travis?
sentences.zh: 迈克，你报道特拉维斯多久了？

sentences.en: I've been writing about Travis since I joined the Times.
sentences.zh: 自从我加入《时报》以来，我就一直在写关于特拉维斯的事情。

sentences.en: I've been at the Times three years ago, almost to the day.
sentences.zh: 我来到《时报》已经三年了，几乎就是整整三年前的今天。

sentences.en: So what was it like for you to get this news on Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 所以在周二听到这个消息对你来说是什么感觉？

sentences.en: You've been such a big part of of covering the scandals that led up to this really significant moment.
sentences.zh: 你一直在深度报道导致这一重大时刻的种种丑闻。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just one of those things where I don't think anyone involved in this whole thing knew
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这件事就像那种直到周二晚上10点半我收到特拉维斯的声明之前，

sentences.en: where it was going to go until Tuesday night at 1030 when I got the statement from Travis.
sentences.zh: 谁也不知道事情会走向何方的时刻。

sentences.en: So it's been kind of insane.
sentences.zh: 所以这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But I think that's kind of the story of Uber that it's crazy and unpredictable.
sentences.zh: 但我想这就是 Uber 的故事所在——疯狂且不可预测。

sentences.en: And we don't know where we are until we finally land somewhere.
sentences.zh: 在我们最终尘埃落定之前，谁也不知道我们身在何方。

sentences.en: All right, Mike, thanks again.
sentences.zh: 好了，迈克，再次谢谢你。

sentences.en: Really appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.en: Talk to you later.
sentences.zh: 回头聊。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 The Reframers，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会当 DJ 时，你每天晚上都要带着300张最珍贵的唱片去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a
sentences.zh: 你把一个

sentences.en: DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: DJ 台变成了一个充满美妙50年历史藏品的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼（Audemars Piguet）的 The Reframers。

sentences.en: Subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today, and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 订阅《纽约时报》，立即下载《时报》应用，即可享受30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Last year, a shocking photo shared on Facebook was seen by millions of people.
sentences.zh: 去年，一张在脸书上分享的令人震惊的照片被数百万人看到。

sentences.en: It shows two adults overdosed on heroin slumped over in the front seat of a car.
sentences.zh: 照片里显示两个成年人海洛因过量，瘫倒在汽车前座上。

sentences.en: A four-year-old boy sits behind them in a car seat, staring straight into the camera.
sentences.zh: 一个四岁的小男孩坐在后座的安全座椅上，直直地盯着镜头。

sentences.en: The photo was taken by a police officer in East Liverpool, Ohio, and published online by the police department.
sentences.zh: 这张照片是由俄亥俄州东利物浦的一名警官拍摄的，并由警察局发布在网上。

sentences.en: They called it a cry for help.
sentences.zh: 他们称这是对救助的呼喊。

sentences.en: You see that photo, you cannot forget it.
sentences.zh: 你看到那张照片，就绝对忘不掉。

sentences.en: Nathaniel Popper has been covering the opioid crisis for The Times.
sentences.zh: 内森·波珀一直在为《时报》报道阿片类药物危机。

sentences.en: You know, I think part of what that photo probably brought home for a lot of people is the degree to which this overdose epidemic has sort of spread to these parts of society
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为那张照片可能让许多人真正意识到的是，这种药物过量流行蔓延到了社会的哪些地方，

sentences.en: that I don't think we used to associate with drugs and overdoses.
sentences.zh: 这些地方以前是不会让人联想到毒品和药物过量的。

sentences.en: You know, this was not some strung out guy in a park.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不是公园里那种精神萎靡的家伙。

sentences.en: And I think just so many parts of that photo just spoke to how far this has all gone.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这张照片的很多方面都说明了这一切已经发展到了何种地步。

sentences.en: This thing just keeps getting worse and worse every year.
sentences.zh: 这事一年比一年更糟。

sentences.en: And we're at a point where this has become essentially the leading cause of death for people under 50 in the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且我们现在面临的情况是，这基本上成了美国50岁以下人群的首要死因。

sentences.en: For me personally, it's one of those photos that came to define the crisis for me.
sentences.zh: 对我个人而言，这是那些定义了这场危机的照片之一。

sentences.en: And so I think it's one of those things that pops into my mind whenever this topic comes up again.
sentences.zh: 所以每当这个话题再次出现时，它就会浮现在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: Yes, it was my police department.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是我们警察局的。

sentences.en: I remember even seeing it for the first time and I'm like, oh my God.
sentences.zh: 我记得第一次看到它时，我心里想，哦天哪。

sentences.en: I called patrolman Chris Green, who works for the East Liverpool Police Department.
sentences.zh: 我给在东利物浦警察局工作的巡警克里斯·格林打了个电话。

sentences.en: But since that picture was published on Facebook, many police departments across the country follow suit and publish pictures very similar.
sentences.zh: 但自从那张照片在脸书上发布后，全国许多警察局都效仿并发布了非常相似的照片。

sentences.en: So thinking about that scene that your colleague walked up on when he took that photo, is that a pretty common thing for you to run into?
sentences.zh: 所以在回想你同事拍那张照片时碰到的场景，这在你们日常工作中很常见吗？

sentences.en: Very.
sentences.zh: 非常常见。

sentences.en: It's nearly a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 几乎每天都有。

sentences.en: And sometimes it's multiple times a day, nearly every shift.
sentences.zh: 有时一天好几次，几乎每个班次都有。

sentences.en: We have three shifts here, you know, typical daylight, afternoon, midnight.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有三个班次，你知道的，常规的白班、下午班、夜班。

sentences.en: Not always kids are involved.
sentences.zh: 并不总是涉及小孩子。

sentences.en: But yesterday, the day before, I responded to an overdose.
sentences.zh: 但昨天，前天，我都处理了一起药物过量事件。

sentences.en: Broad daylight, middle of the sidewalk, guy just laying there, dying.
sentences.zh: 大白天，人行道正中间，一个家伙就那么躺着，快要死了。

sentences.en: And I believe he said like the fifth time he's overdosed.
sentences.zh: 而且我想他说这已经是第五次药物过量了。

sentences.en: Sometimes several times a day, people drive and people wrecking into telephone poles.
sentences.zh: 有时一天好几次，有人开车撞到电线杆上。

sentences.en: Last week we had one overdose and he was climbing a telephone pole like he was possessed.
sentences.zh: 上周我们处理了一起过量事件，那家伙像着了魔一样往电线杆上爬。

sentences.en: And we have a huge issue with the whole drug epidemic.
sentences.zh: 我们整个毒品流行问题非常严重。

sentences.en: That is, that's what we deal with more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们处理得最多的事情，比其他任何事都多。

sentences.en: I think part of what we've seen is this progression through the opioid crisis.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们所看到的一部分是阿片类药物危机的这种发展历程。

sentences.en: And I think this really began with prescription pills, Percocet, Oxycodone, things like that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这确实是从处方止痛药开始的，比如羟考酮、Percocet之类的东西。

sentences.en: And you've seen this steady line of prescription pill overdose deaths increasing over the last 10 or 20 years as the drug companies have pushed these pills out as pain relief.
sentences.zh: 随着制药公司将这些药作为止痛药推向市场，在过去10到20年里，你可以看到处方药过量致死的数量在稳步上升。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people saw that when authorities started to crack down on prescription pill prescriptions,
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都看到了，当当局开始严厉打击处方药开具时，

sentences.en: people who were addicted to these things needed something to get their fix.
sentences.zh: 对这些东西上瘾的人需要别的东西来解瘾。

sentences.en: And so they moved to heroin firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们首先转向了海洛因。

sentences.en: And so you saw this really dramatic spike in heroin overdose deaths over the last decade.
sentences.zh: 因此在过去十年里，海洛因过量致死人数出现了非常戏剧性的激增。

sentences.en: But really what we're in the middle of right now, I think, is a third wave in this overdose crisis and can be traced pretty squarely to these synthetic opioids like fentanyl.
sentences.zh: 但实际上我们现在正处于这场药物过量危机的第三波浪潮中，我认为这完全可以追溯到芬太尼这种合成阿片类药物。

sentences.en: Fentanyl, that's the most widely distributed, the most popular one that's out there, that are something like 50 times as potent and powerful as heroin.
sentences.zh: 芬太尼，这是分发最广、最受欢迎的一种，其药效和威力大约是海洛因的50倍。

sentences.en: And this has become the core of the overdose crisis, I think, right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这已经成为当前药物过量危机的核心。

sentences.en: We see that more than anything.
sentences.zh: 我们看到最多的就是这个。

sentences.en: We see very little cocaine.
sentences.zh: 我们很少看到可卡因。

sentences.en: We're actually starting to see very little heroin.
sentences.zh: 我们其实也开始很少看到海洛因了。

sentences.en: Most of everything that we're getting is fentanyl.
sentences.zh: 我们搞到的绝大多数东西都是芬太尼。

sentences.en: We've recently discovered a new strand of fentanyl, and then we've even had several occasions of carfentanyl.
sentences.zh: 我们最近发现了一种新的芬太尼品种，甚至还有好几次遇到了卡芬太尼。

sentences.en: And when did this become the it drug?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是什么时候成为最火的毒品的？

sentences.en: When did it become so popular?
sentences.zh: 它是什么时候变得这么受欢迎的？

sentences.en: In this particular area, just over a year ago.
sentences.zh: 在这个特定地区，就在一年多前。

sentences.en: When that picture was published, that was about the time when we started seeing the transition.
sentences.zh: 当那张照片被发表时，差不多就是我们开始看到转变的时候。

sentences.en: We started seeing heroin laced with fentanyl.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到掺有芬太尼的海洛因。

sentences.en: And now on this particular incident, May 12th, I'm literally walking into the gym for an evening lift.
sentences.zh: 而在这次具体的事件中，5月12日，我正准备去健身房进行晚上的力量训练。

sentences.en: And it's Friday evening.
sentences.zh: 那是星期五晚上。

sentences.en: I have a nice three-day weekend, and I'm just going to spend the weekend hunting.
sentences.zh: 我有一个美好的三天周末，我打算把周末花在打猎上。

sentences.en: I get a phone call from Rob Smith, Officer Smith, and he says, hey, I just seen Justin Buckwell do a hand-to-hand.
sentences.zh: 我接到了罗布·史密斯警官的电话，他说，嘿，我刚看到贾斯汀·巴克韦尔进行了一次直接交易。

sentences.en: So we immediately drop what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们立刻放下手头的事。

sentences.en: We're in unmarked cars.
sentences.zh: 我们开着便衣警车。

sentences.en: We call our uniformed officers, and they're like, yeah, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我们打电话给穿制服的警察，他们说，行，上吧。

sentences.en: Let's get them stopped.
sentences.zh: 把他们截停。

sentences.en: So they find a reason to stop him.
sentences.zh: 于是他们找了个理由截停了他。

sentences.en: And uniformed officers have the lights on.
sentences.zh: 穿制服的警察亮起了警灯。

sentences.en: They have him at gunpoint.
sentences.zh: 他们用枪指着他。

sentences.en: And the two, Justin Buckwell and Cortez Collins, begin to rip open these bags of white powder,
sentences.zh: 然后这两个人，贾斯汀·巴克韦尔和科尔特斯·柯林斯，开始撕开这些装有白色粉末的袋子，

sentences.en: thinking, you know, it's cocaine or something of that nature, just because how pure and white it is.
sentences.zh: 心想，你知道的，这是可卡因或类似的东西，纯粹是因为它看起来又纯又白。

sentences.en: So I go to Justin's cruiser, and he sweat profusely.
sentences.zh: 于是我走到贾斯汀的巡逻车旁，他满头大汗。

sentences.en: I mean, he looks like, have you ever seen the show Walking Dead?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他看起来，你看过《行尸走肉》这部剧吗？

sentences.en: How those people just don't look.
sentences.zh: 那些人看起来就很不对劲。

sentences.en: Okay, even a commercial.
sentences.zh: 好吧，哪怕是广告里的。

sentences.en: It's a zombie show, right?
sentences.zh: 那是部丧尸剧，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: These people, they're walking zombies.
sentences.zh: 这些人，他们就是行尸走肉。

sentences.en: They don't eat.
sentences.zh: 他们不吃东西。

sentences.en: They don't drink.
sentences.zh: 他们不喝水。

sentences.en: They don't take care of themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们不照顾自己。

sentences.en: So as I'm talking to Justin at this point, Justin Buckwell, he says it's cocaine.
sentences.zh: 所以当我在此时跟贾斯汀谈话时，贾斯汀·巴克韦尔说这是可卡因。

sentences.en: And then finally he comes clean and says it's fentanyl.
sentences.zh: 然后他终于坦白了，说这是芬太尼。

sentences.en: So we get him back to the station, and we're kind of high-fiving because, you know, we knew that we just disrupted a big drug deal.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把他带回了警局，我们甚至击掌庆祝，因为，你知道的，我们知道我们刚刚破获了一起大毒品交易。

sentences.en: And as I'm walking out the door, a captain of mine was like, hey, you have something on your shirt, on the back of your shirt.
sentences.zh: 当我正要走出门口时，我的一个队长说，嘿，你衬衫上有东西，衬衫背面有东西。

sentences.en: I'm like, yeah, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我说，行吧，无所谓。

sentences.en: And I kind of instinctively flick it off with my thumb.
sentences.zh: 我本能地用大拇指把它弹掉。

sentences.en: Within two minutes, I fall into the door, and that's the last thing I remember.
sentences.zh: 两分钟内，我倒在了门上，那是我的最后记忆。

sentences.en: Next thing I remember is waking up in the hospital and looking around and seeing my colleagues full-grown men, the nurses, EMTs, firemen, my fiancée, in tears and very upset.
sentences.zh: 我恢复记忆时发现自己在医院里，环顾四周，看到我的同事们——都是成年男子，还有护士、急救人员、消防员、我的未婚妻——泪流满面，非常难过。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking, what in the hell are you guys doing here?
sentences.zh: 我在想，你们到底在搞什么鬼？

sentences.en: And they're like, you overdosed.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你药物过量了。

sentences.en: I'm like, get out of here.
sentences.zh: 我说，别开玩笑了。

sentences.en: You overdosed just by touching the back of your shirt to see what was on it?
sentences.zh: 你仅仅因为用后背摸了一下衬衫想看看上面有什么就药物过量了？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That was all it took?
sentences.zh: 只需要这样？

sentences.en: That's all it took.
sentences.zh: 只需要这样。

sentences.en: You see a lot of people referring to it as a chemical weapon, and I don't think that's an unreasonable comparison.
sentences.zh: 你看到很多人把它称为生化武器，我认为这个比喻并不过分。

sentences.en: Actually, I think the Russian military used some form of it when there was a hostage crisis
sentences.zh: 实际上，我认为俄罗斯军方在几年前发生某起人质危机时就使用过某种形式的这种东西，

sentences.en: at this theater some years ago, and they pumped it into the theater to knock everybody out immediately.
sentences.zh: 当时他们在剧院里注入了这种气体，让所有人都立刻昏迷了过去。

sentences.en: It was essentially a sort of chemical weapon in that setting.
sentences.zh: 在那种环境下，它基本上就是一种生化武器。

sentences.en: And that's sort of the role it's playing in America right now, the number of deaths it's causing.
sentences.zh: 这就是它目前在美利坚扮演的角色，它造成的死亡人数惊人。

sentences.en: And I think part of what's so striking about the rise of fentanyl is how quickly it has made heroin just seem like this kind of tame recreational drug.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为芬太尼的崛起最令人震惊的一部分在于，它以多快的速度把海洛因衬托得就像一种温和的娱乐性毒品。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, just the way in which fentanyl can show up in a place where people are already dying
sentences.zh: 我是说，芬太尼出现在人们本来就在因海洛因致死的地方的方式，然后你就会遇到基本上类似于大规模死亡事件的情况，许多人

sentences.en: of heroin, and then you'll just get essentially like a mass death event where a bunch of people
sentences.zh: 根本没有接触过芬太尼，可能并不知道它被掺入了他们的海洛因中。

sentences.en: who had had no exposure to fentanyl maybe weren't aware that it was being cut into their heroin.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个周末内一个小城市里就会有15人死亡。

sentences.en: You know, 15 people will die in a small city in a weekend.
sentences.zh: 我的天呐。

sentences.en: My goodness.
sentences.zh: 你看到全国各地的警察都在大城市里谈论这个，到处都是尸体。

sentences.en: And you're seeing cops talk about this in cities across the country, and you just get bodies everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很疯狂，但到什么时候才算够了，难道我们要穿着生化防护服去接警和进行交通拦截吗，否则我们很多人都会送命。

sentences.en: It sounds crazy, but at what point is enough enough, and we're going to have to answer
sentences.zh: 这东西和炭疽一样危险。

sentences.en: calls and traffic stops and biohazard suits, or a lot of us are going to end up dead.
sentences.zh: 它和任何东西一样危险。

sentences.en: This stuff is as dangerous as anthrax.
sentences.zh: 如果我把这东西寄给你，它杀死你的速度会比炭疽还快。

sentences.en: It's as dangerous as anything.
sentences.zh: 人们是从哪弄来芬太尼的？

sentences.en: If I mail you this stuff, it's going to kill you quicker than anthrax.
sentences.zh: 我们看到它来自更高级的大毒枭，我们大部分的东西都是从克利夫兰和哥伦布运过来的。

sentences.en: Where are people getting fentanyl?
sentences.zh: 克利夫兰在我们以北大约两小时车程处。

sentences.en: We are seeing it from higher drug kingpins, and most of our stuff is being shipped in from
sentences.zh: 哥伦布在我市以西大约三到三个半小时车程处。

sentences.en: Cleveland and Columbus.
sentences.zh: 但能查获纯海洛因、纯可卡因或纯快克，几乎让人有一种松了一口气的感觉。

sentences.en: Cleveland is about two hours north of us.
sentences.zh: 这么说挺让人痛心的，你知道的。

sentences.en: Columbus is about three to three and a half hours west of us.
sentences.zh: 但毒品的真正来源可能要遥远得多，超出了格林巡警的控制范围。

sentences.en: But it's almost a sign of relief to find just heroin or just cocaine or just crack.
sentences.zh: 在本故事的第二部分中，我们将探讨芬太尼的来源。

sentences.en: And then that's sad to say, you know.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: But the real source of the drugs is probably much farther away, outside Patrolman Green's control.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿是时候迎来新的领导层了。

sentences.en: In part two of this story, where the fentanyl is coming from.
sentences.zh: 我认为华盛顿和民主党是时候迎来新一代的领导层了。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚州特别选举中遭遇令人失望的失败后，民主党人正仓促重新集结。

sentences.en: It's time for new leadership in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们现今的一些领导人，大多在70岁中期到后期，我认为是时候退居二线了。

sentences.en: I think it's time for a new generation of leadership in Washington and in the Democratic
sentences.zh: 是时候注入一些新鲜血液了。

sentences.en: Party.
sentences.zh: 这次失利重新引发了对该党的担忧，一些成员质疑众议院少数党领袖南希·佩洛西的领导地位，另一些人则称民主党本身的品牌已经变得有毒。

sentences.en: Democrats are scrambling to regroup after a disappointing defeat in a Georgia special election.
sentences.zh: 来自俄亥俄州的众议员蒂姆·莱恩周三对《时报》表示，我们的品牌比特朗普还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Some of the leadership that we have today, mostly in their mid to late 70s, it's, I think, time to move on.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克军队指责极端组织“伊斯兰国”摧毁了伊拉克最著名的地标之一，即摩苏尔老城的一座拥有数百年历史的清真寺，摩苏尔战役的最后阶段目前正是在那里进行。

sentences.en: It's time for some fresh blood.
sentences.zh: 这也是“伊斯兰国”头目阿布·贝克尔·巴格达迪于2014年宣布建立哈里发国的地方。

sentences.en: The loss has revived concerns about the party, with some members questioning the leadership of House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi, and others saying the Democratic brand itself has
sentences.zh: “伊斯兰国”将此次袭击归咎于美军空袭。

sentences.en: become toxic.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日简报》的全部内容。

sentences.en: Our brand is worse than Trump, Representative Tim Ryan of Ohio told The Times on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 我是凯特琳·迪克森。

sentences.en: And the Iraqi army is accusing ISIS of destroying one of Iraq's most famous landmarks, a centuries-old
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: mosque in Mosul's old city, where the final phase of the battle for Mosul is being fought.
